column1: # advertised-features.tsv — the ONE list of features this product's releases
# document as present, and the build options that must hold for that claim to be
# true. tests/release-honesty-gate.sh reads this file and nothing else: the gate
# carries no feature list of its own, so there is no second copy to drift from
# the release notes.
# WHAT THIS FILE EXISTS TO PREVENT (kept from the v0.1.0-alpha defect, because it
# is the reason the gate exists): the published v0.1.0-alpha advertised "VST3 and
# CLAP hosting, effects only" while all seven jobs of its release run printed
# "VST3 hosting skipped: no SDK" / "CLAP hosting skipped: no headers" and shipped
# neither. Both options default to AUTO, and AUTO with the dependency absent is a
# skip with a STATUS line — a silent compile-out that no test noticed.
# CHANGED FOR 0.2.0-alpha — the rows below are the 0.2.0 contract:
#   * vst3-instrument-hosting is NEW. The host module is plugins/Vst3Instrument,
#     whose target is BUILD_PLUGIN(vst3instrument ...) and which is gated by
#     WANT_VST3 — the SAME option the effect host uses, which the release jobs
#     already pass as -DWANT_VST3=ON. It is deliberately NOT gated by
#     WANT_VST3_TEST_INSTRUMENT: that option (default OFF) builds the MIT
#     test-instrument FIXTURE, a test asset, and is a row of its own below so the
#     two cannot be confused in either direction.
#   * the 0.2.0 release notes must therefore describe instrument hosting with the
#     limits we actually measured: one instrument per track, MIDI in to audio out;
#     no third-party instrument has been run (the witness is the in-tree MIT
#     fixture); the plugin's own editor does not open, so its parameters surface
#     as a generated grid; no multi-out, no presets, no instrument latency in PDC,
#     no out-of-process hosting.
# A NOTE ON WHY `session-view` IS A ROW WITH required=OFF, WHICH IS NOT A SNUB.
# `OPTION(WANT_SESSION_VIEW "..." OFF)` (CMakeLists.txt:121) defaults OFF and the
# release jobs do not pass it, so the Session View data layer and the launch
# scheduler that builds on it are IN THE TREE BUT NOT IN THIS BUILD. Recording it
# as a row means the release CANNOT drift into claiming a clip launcher it does not
# contain: the day a build turns the option on, this gate fails and the notes have
# to be updated first. CORRECTED 2026-09-12: the wording here used to say "even with the flag ON the audit
# found no consumer", which was true when that audit ran and is true no longer — the launch scheduler
# (src/core/SessionScheduler.cpp, merged in this release) is a consumer behind this flag. What remains
# accurate, and is the claim this row protects: there is still no CLIP LAUNCHER — no scene launcher and no
# clip grid, both being UI the scheduler does not have. So the honest description of 0.2.0-alpha is that the
# session data layer AND its launch scheduler exist in the source, ship disabled, and are not operable.
# WHY THERE IS NO ROW FOR TELEMETRY, THOUGH THE RELEASE DOCUMENTS IT.
# The gate can only judge what the binary REPORTS, and the build-options string is assembled by
# src/CMakeLists.txt from variables matching `^WANT|LMMS_(HAVE|DEBUG)`. The telemetry kill switch is
# `ZENE_TELEMETRY` (default ON) and it matches neither pattern, so it never reaches `lmms --version` —
# and a row for an option the build does not report is a FAIL by this gate's own rule. Two ways to close
# it, both post-release: expose a `LMMS_HAVE_TELEMETRY` flag into the dump (which also lets a user tell
# whether their binary contains the client), or widen the CMake pattern. Until then telemetry is
# documented in prose and guarded by its own tests, not by this contract.
# WHY THERE IS NO ROW FOR THE VST3 TEST-INSTRUMENT FIXTURE — and the reason is NOT what this note first said.
# The first version claimed the option "is declared inside tests/CMakeLists.txt under a condition, so it never
# reaches the generated header". A merge train proved that FALSE on 2026-09-12: its tree's `build/lmmsversion.h`
# reports `WANT_VST3_TEST_INSTRUMENT='OFF'`. The real mechanism is subtler and worse. The dump is assembled in
# `src/CMakeLists.txt` through `get_cmake_property(_define_vars VARIABLES)`, which runs BEFORE
# `ADD_SUBDIRECTORY(tests)` — so on a FRESH configure the option does not exist yet and is absent from the dump;
# but `option()` writes a CACHE variable, so on any later configure of the same build directory it is already
# defined at that point and DOES land in the dump. Consequence: **the same source tree can export two different
# `LMMS_BUILD_OPTIONS` strings depending on the build directory's history.** A row for this option would
# therefore pass or fail according to how many times a directory had been configured, which is worse than having
# no row — the guard's job is to describe the build, not the build directory's biography. The fixture is a test
# asset documented in prose; that is the whole claim.
# GENERAL CAVEAT THIS EXPOSES, which belongs with the guard rather than only here: the dump is a function of the
# source tree AND the build directory's configure history. All six rows below use options declared at the TOP
# LEVEL of `CMakeLists.txt`, so they are present either way — but any future row for a nested or conditionally
# declared option must be verified on a FRESH configure before it is trusted.
# Columns (TAB separated):
#   1 feature   stable id, printed by the gate
#   2 option    the WANT_* option the binary reports in its "Build options:" dump
#   3 required  the value that must hold: ON, OFF, or an exact string
#   4 module    plugin module basename to find in the build tree ('-' for none)
#   5 claim     the sentence this row keeps true, quoted when the gate fails
# A feature documented as ABSENT is a row too (required OFF). If a build turns one
# on, the documents understate that build and the release is dishonest in the other
# direction, so the gate fails on it as well.
vst3-hosting
